strategy.thesis: Self-described as the most active fintech investor in Southeast Asia; leads pre-seed and seed rounds for fintech founders building financial rails, plus enterprise AI and automated workflows.

summary.en: Singapore-based early-stage VC, established in early 2020, focused on seed-stage fintech across Southeast Asia (with selective bets in Pakistan and Bangladesh); self-described as the most active fintech investor in the region.

summary.en: Singapore-based early-stage VC founded in 2017 (formerly Dymon Asia Ventures), investing from pre-Series A to Series B in fintech, healthtech and climate companies that embed financial services, across Southeast and South Asia. Manages over US$140M across two funds.

strategy.thesis: Venture arm of Credit Saison (a US$30B AUM financial-services conglomerate); though mandate is sector-agnostic, prefers founders building platforms or ecosystems that distribute financial services to the underbanked. Onigiri Capital targets stablecoins, payments, asset tokenization, DeFi and financial infrastructure.

summary.en: Singapore-based corporate venture arm of Japan's Credit Saison, formed in 2019 as a ~US$150M evergreen fund investing seed-to-Series A across Southeast Asia and India, with a thesis centred on distributing financial services to the underbanked. In 2025 launched Onigiri Capital, a US$50M blockchain/fintech fund.

strategy.thesis: Corporate VC of Kasikornbank (KBANK); invests in early-to-growth-stage tech startups in financial technology, consumer internet and enterprise technology, themed around the Future of Finance, Commerce, Living and Impact.

summary.en: Bangkok-based corporate VC wholly owned by Kasikornbank (KBANK), founded in 2017. Started with a $30M fund and expanded to $255M in 2022, investing across fintech, consumer internet and enterprise tech in Thailand and Southeast Asia.

summary.en: Singapore-based fintech private-credit investment platform incorporated in 2018, deploying senior secured loans and equity into Asia-based fintech lenders and non-bank financial institutions. Has deployed over US$500M cumulatively as of mid-2025.

strategy.thesis: Corporate VC of Bank Mandiri, Indonesia's largest financial group; the first local bank to launch a dedicated fintech venture fund, investing primarily in fintech startups and acting as a bridge between the Mandiri Group and startups.

summary.en: Jakarta-based corporate VC of Bank Mandiri, founded in 2015 as the first Indonesian bank-backed fintech venture fund (initial US$37M budget). Focuses on financing fintech startups across Indonesia and Southeast Asia; ~48 portfolio companies as of April 2024.
summary.local: Lengan modal ventura korporat (CVC) milik Bank Mandiri, didirikan tahun 2015, berfokus pada pendanaan startup fintech di Indonesia dan Asia Tenggara.

sources.title: How 4 Indonesian Banks are Collaborating with Fintech Startups

verification_notes: Founding year cited as 2015 by some sources and 2016 by others (fund launched early 2016 with US$37M budget). Has since added broader vehicles (Balance Sheet Fund, Merah Putih Fund, Indonesia Impact Fund), but the core mandate and identity remain fintech-focused.

strategy.thesis: Corporate VC of Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI); leverages BRI's financial-sector network, focusing on fintech and its ecosystem (with the Sembrani Nusantara fund targeting early-stage fintech for MSMEs), later broadening into agriculture, health, retail and logistics.

summary.en: Jakarta-based corporate VC of state-owned Bank Rakyat Indonesia, launched in 2019 with an IDR 3.5 trillion (US$250M) allocation, focusing on fintech and its ecosystem. Runs the OJK-regulated Sembrani Nusantara fund (targeting early-stage fintech for MSMEs).
summary.local: Lengan modal ventura korporat milik Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI), diluncurkan tahun 2019 dengan alokasi Rp 3,5 triliun, berfokus pada fintech dan ekosistemnya.

strategy.thesis: Global venture studio for inclusive fintech: uses the venture-studio model to build repeatable, scalable, profitable fintechs that bridge financial inclusion for underserved, underrepresented groups.

Raised US$5M from Chemonics International in 2023 and a $7.5M Series A in 2026; portfolio includes BayaniPay, Higala and Asenso Finance.
